title: Specialized inverse-image comparison square for open exchange
statement: For every finite commutative ring Λ, chosen Cartesian square gU:U′→U, j′:U′→X′, j:U→X, g:X′→X with gU≫j=j′≫g, and etale Λ-module sheaf F on X, let rho_f=comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso Λ f. Then rho_gU.inv at j_et^*F, followed by gU_pro^*(rho_j.inv at F), followed by upperStarCompIso Λ sq.w at nu_X^*F, equals nu_U′^* of the component of Etale.squareUpperStarIso Λ sq.toCommSq.flip at F, followed by rho_j′.inv at g_et^*F, followed by j′_pro^*(rho_g.inv at F). All maps are the specified canonical comparison maps. No open-immersion assumption is required.

source.place: Tags 099R and 0B65; compatibility of the etale/pro-etale inverse-image comparison with a chosen Cartesian square.

proof.text: Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$, $P_f=f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$, $E_f=f_{\mathrm{et}}^*$, and $w:g_U\mathbin{\gg}j=j'\mathbin{\gg}g$. Flip the chosen square, obtaining $s'$ with edges $(j',g_U,g,j)$ and commutativity $w^{-1}$. Its chosen pullback identification is the given $U'\simeq U\times_X X'$ followed by the map $U\times_X X'\to X'\times_X U$ exchanging the projections. This map is an isomorphism: the reverse exchange is its inverse, since each composite has the two identity projections and the fibre-product universal property makes it the identity. The projection equations for $s'$ are the original two equations in the opposite order. Thus the flipped data really are a chosen Cartesian square, with no condition on $j$ or $j'$.

proof.text: Apply [stage3-proetale-comparison-square-component] with the same commutative ring $\Lambda$, the flipped square $s'$, and $F$ on its lower-right corner $X$. Let $d=\operatorname{comparisonSquareData}(\operatorname{ModuleCat}\Lambda,s')$. The cited conclusion is precisely $\operatorname{ComparisonSquareComponent}(d,F)$. This is applicable to every commutative ring, hence in particular to the finite commutative ring here. The remaining steps identify its specified fields; they do not replace the canonical comparison by an arbitrary natural isomorphism.

proof.text: The canonical coefficient comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] is $c_f:N_{\operatorname{dom}f}E_f\simeq P_fN_{\operatorname{cod}f}$. In the named construction, $c_f=\operatorname{comparisonCoefficientPullbackIso}(\Lambda,f)=\rho_f^{-1}$: unfolding the two definitions gives the same inverse under the conjugate-isomorphism equivalence of the same restriction direct-image isomorphism. For the flipped square, direct substitution in the definition of $d$ gives $(L_1,L_2,L'_1,L'_2)=(E_j,E_{g_U},E_g,E_{j'})$, $(R_1,R_2,R'_1,R'_2)=(P_j,P_{g_U},P_g,P_{j'})$, and $(K_0,K_1,K'_1,K_2)=(N_X,N_U,N_{X'},N_{U'})$. Its four coefficient fields $(c_2,c_1,c'_2,c'_1)$ are respectively $(\rho_{g_U}^{-1},\rho_j^{-1},\rho_{j'}^{-1},\rho_g^{-1})$. This is an unfolding of the chosen maps, not an appeal to uniqueness without normalization.

proof.text: For either site, write $C(f,h):(f\mathbin{\gg}h)^*\simeq h^*\mathbin{\gg}f^*$ (with functor composition written in application order) for its canonical composition comparison. By definition its square field for $s'$ is $C(g_U,j)^{-1}$, then equality transport along $w$, then $C(j',g)$. For the etale site this is exactly $\operatorname{Etale.squareUpperStarIso}(\Lambda,s'.\operatorname{toCommSq})$. To check the convention for a comparison $h=f\mathbin{\gg}g$, substitute this equality: the general etale composition comparison is equality transport from $h^*$ followed by $C(f,g)$; when the equality is reflexive, the transport is the identity. Associativity and $(ab)^{-1}=b^{-1}a^{-1}$ then give the displayed square expression. For the pro-etale site the same expression is, by its definition, $\operatorname{upperStarCompIso}(\Lambda,w)$. Here $(s'.w)^{-1}=w$ by equality-proof irrelevance, so the specified commutativity proof is retained. Thus $d.se$ is the etale square of $\operatorname{sq.toCommSq.flip}$ and $d.sp$ is the pro-etale square attached to the original $w$.

proof.text: Unfold only the component predicate obtained in step 2. It reads $d.c_2(F\text{ after }L_1)\gg R_2(d.c_1(F))\gg d.sp(K_0F)=K_2(d.se(F))\gg d.c'_2(L'_1F)\gg R'_2(d.c'_1(F))$, where each isomorphism denotes its hom component. Substitute the fields listed in steps 3 and 4, and use $(\rho_f^{-1}).\mathrm{hom}=\rho_f.\mathrm{inv}$. The left side is $\rho_{g_U}^{-1}(E_jF)\gg P_{g_U}(\rho_j^{-1}(F))\gg\operatorname{upperStarCompIso}(\Lambda,w)(N_XF)$. The right side is $N_{U'}(\operatorname{Etale.squareUpperStarIso}(\Lambda,\operatorname{sq.toCommSq.flip})(F))\gg\rho_{j'}^{-1}(E_gF)\gg P_{j'}(\rho_g^{-1}(F))$. These are exactly the specified two composites in the statement. Both composites have source $N_{U'}E_{g_U}E_jF$ and target $P_{j'}P_gN_XF$.

lean.statement: theorem fixSiteOpenExchangeSquare (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {U' U X' X : Scheme.{u}} {gU : U' ⟶ U} {j' : U' ⟶ X'} {j : U ⟶ X} {g : X' ⟶ X} (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare gU j' j g) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) : (comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) gU).inv.app ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).obj F) ≫ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) gU).map ((comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).inv.app F) ≫ (upperStarCompIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) sq.w).hom.app ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) X).obj F) = (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) U').map ((Etale.squareUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) sq.toCommSq.flip).hom.app F) ≫ (comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j').inv.app ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).obj F) ≫ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j').map ((comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).inv.app F)
